messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT OPENED: Elevated 5xx rate for /v1/generate (hosted) — detected by uptime-checker. Paging eng-oncall@pager. Severity: P1.
emily: seeing it, joining. grabbing dashboard and logs.
emily: error spike started ~2856001200, 5xx rate jumped from ~0.4% to ~7.8% across gen-inference pool. latency also up.
sara: any recent deploys? deploy-bot: deploys: no user-facing deploys in last 30m, infra autoscaler scaled a few nodes at 2856001105.
ryan: i'm watching model-runner logs on pool-3. getting repeated segfaults and OOM python deaths, then kube restarting pods. sample: 
```
[2024-11-02T15:02:11Z] model-runner[pid=4321] SIGSEGV at 0x8
[2024-11-02T15:02:11Z] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 4321 (python) total-vm:10240000kB, anon-rss:8120000kB
```
ryan: looks like runtime hitting large memory growth during KV cache refill.
emily: confirmed — metrics show a subset of requests with long context lengths triggering OOMs. Could be new large-context prefix causing page allocations.
matt: are these only on GPU nodes or CPU fallbacks too?
ryan: primarily on gpu-pool-3 (A100s), but when node crashes requests fall back to smaller CPU runners which have much higher latency and also start timing out (cascading).
emily: mitigation plan — 1) route traffic away from gpu-pool-3 via routing override, 2) enable fallback-model variant (smaller quantized model) as default for hosted for next 10m, 3) drain pods on gpu-pool-3 and restart nodes after collecting core dumps.
sara: +1. I'm going to flip routing. doing: `POST /admin/routing/override {"pool":"gpu-pool-3","weight":0}`
sara: @ops-bot drain started for gpu-pool-3 nodes. collecting logs to s3://redwood-incidents/2856001234/
ops-bot: Drain request accepted. Nodes marked DRAINING: 3 nodes in gpu-pool-3.
emily: enabling quantized fallback: `PATCH /admin/models/gen-1/routing {"variant":"gen-1-quant","weight":1.0}` — applied. Expect reduced quality but keeps requests flowing.
ryan: restarting model-runner on one crashed pod to capture core: `kubectl -n inference exec -it model-runner-7 -- bash -c 'gcore -o /tmp/core.$(hostname) $(pidof python) && tar -czf /tmp/logs.tgz /var/log/model-runner && aws s3 cp /tmp/core.* s3://redwood-incidents/2856001234/'`
emily: good. also lowering concurrent requests per worker to avoid large batching: `set-config concurrency 1` on pool.
matt: can we also temporarily disable KV cache for long-context requests? that might stop the memory blowup.
sara: there's a config flag: `--kv-cache=false` — applying to the canary node first.
sara: applied to canary; monitoring.
ryan: can confirm the segfaults stopped on canary after disabling kv-cache. 5xx rate on canary dropped to baseline.
emily: pushing routing to send 90% to fallback quantized and 10% to canary with kv-cache disabled.
ryan: noting customer impact: hosted API 95th latency from 230ms -> 1.6s during peak, 5xx increased to 7.8% for last 5m. No signed enterprise SLA breaches yet but a couple of users reported timeouts.
emily: alert board — post a short customer message on status page: "Degraded performance for text generation endpoints; mitigation in progress. No data loss." I'll draft after we stabilize.
matt: on-call handoff note in 10m: if you need to step out, summarize actions and state.
emily: collecting summary: root cause likely regression in runtime memory growth when KV cache refill interacts with long contexts; triggered OOM + segfault on gpu-pool-3 leading to pod evictions and increased fallback to slow CPU runners -> timeouts and higher 5xx. Mitigations applied: routing override away from affected pool, enable smaller quantized model, disable kv-cache on canary, reduce concurrency, drain and restart nodes, captured cores/logs.
sara: cores uploaded: s3://redwood-incidents/2856001234/cores.tar.gz. attached crash stacks show native allocator abort in attention kernel.
emily: tagging infra/research to debug native kernel: @matt please pick up kernel-level analysis.
matt: ack. i'll take post-shift. for now i'll keep paging contact: matt (pager).
emily: last check — 5xx down to ~0.9%, latency back to ~300ms. still watching for regressions.
ryan: note: we also saw one pod show double free in logs prior to crash. saving stack traces.
emily: creating incident ticket INC-285600 on JIRA, severity P1, linking logs and cores. assigning to eng-ml (ryan, matt) and eng-runtime (sara).
emily: handing off to matt for overnight monitoring and root cause. summary for handoff: impact (hosted generation degraded, some customer timeouts), mitigation (traffic routed to quantized variant, affected nodes drained, kv-cache disabled), artifacts (logs, cores, metrics links), next steps (reproduce in staging with long-context workload, fix kernel allocator guard, prepare hotpatch or model runner update).
matt: taking over. I have pager escalation set. I'll post updates in this thread if anything changes.
emily: thanks team. I'll update status page: "Mitigation in progress; partial restoration of service. We will provide a follow-up postmortem." :thumbsup:
incidents-bot: Incident severity downgraded to P2 at 2856001285 (mitigation effective).
matt: quick checklist for follow-ups: 1) reproduce crash in staging with KV refill + long-context synthetic test, 2) audit recent kernel/allocator changes, 3) add guardrails in runtime to cap KV refill memory, 4) run canary rollout of patched runtime, 5) customer postmortem and timeline.
emily: added to INC-285600 epic. closing live remediation loop. we'll reconvene for RCA tomorrow.
